explanation: Build undirected adjacency lists and two-color each connected component using breadth-first search. A neighbor with the same color proves no placement is possible; otherwise assign the opposite color.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: A BFS tree alternates colors on every traversed edge. If an edge joins two equal colors, its endpoints require contradictory assignments, proving an odd cycle. Otherwise every edge joins opposite colors, providing a valid bipartition for each connected component.
walkthrough: For edges 0−1−2−3−0 and isolated vertex 4, color {0,2,4} one color and {1,3} the other. Every edge crosses colors, so all 5 vertices can be placed.
edgeCases: Disconnected and isolated vertices must all be processed.
A self-loop cannot connect opposite groups.
An odd cycle fails; an even cycle does not.
